title: SLA-aware reservation routing and budgeting playbook for Dedicated capacity
creator: Meera Shah
description:
Problem: Sales and platform teams need a consistent, low-friction intake and approval flow for Dedicated capacity reservation requests that (1) enforces SLA/throughput guarantees, (2) maps to autoscaling and fleet control policies, and (3) gives accurate cost and impact estimates for finance and SRE. This ticket delivers a playbook and machine-actionable routing matrix that ties reservation tiers to autoscaling profiles, latency/throughput SLOs, budgeting templates, and approver matrices. Includes intake form fields, eligibility rules, fallback model routing, and audit log requirements.

Scope: intake -> eligibility checks -> cost estimation -> approval routing -> provisioning handoff -> monitoring hooks. Excludes UI mockups (separate design ticket) and infra implementation of autoscaling engine (dependency).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical intake form (CSV and web JSON schema) with required fields: customer, business justification, expected QPS, 95th latency target, peak concurrency windows, data residency, committed term
Routing matrix that deterministically maps requests to reservation tier A/B/C and autoscaling profile (burst vs steady) with documented thresholds
Approval matrix listing roles and SLAs for decisions (sales/solutions/infra/legal/finance), with response SLAs defined
Cost estimator model that outputs monthly committed spend, expected per-token unit cost delta, and breakeven for pay-as-you-go vs reserved
Hand-off checklist for provisioning (networking, KMS, audit, onboarding runbook) and monitoring dashboard links
Runbook for emergency scale-up and graceful degradation with fallback routing to hosted variants
runbook_steps: 1) Intake: customer-facing form submitted; system validates required fields and flags missing items
2) Eligibility check: auto-validate QPS and latency targets against model compatibility and region capacity
3) Cost estimation: run estimator; surface committed vs on-demand comparison and suggested term
4) Routing: assign reservation tier and autoscaling profile; attach recommended fallback model variants
5) Approvals: route to approvers based on tier and customer impact; capture decision and SLA
6) Provisioning handoff: create provisioning ticket for Dedicated team with checklist items (networking, KMS, audit, monitoring), assign ETA
7) Post-provision validation: run synthetic workload, validate SLOs, and finalize customer onboarding notes
8) Ongoing: attach reservation to cost/latency dashboards and schedule quarterly review
decision_log: 2026-03-10: Decided to use deterministic threshold mapping (QPS + 95th latency) rather than fully subjective review for initial routing to reduce turnaround time
2026-03-11: Trade-off: allow limited burst pools for Tier B to improve UX at cost of slightly higher capital reserve; recorded as finance risk
2026-03-12: Agreed on required SLA response times for approvals: 48h for Tier A, 3 business days for Tier B, 7 business days for Tier C
